findings.text: The opening tells a newcomer in plain words what Athena is and that this page is a study it wrote about another project, firstmate. The reader can say what they are looking at within three short paragraphs.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository.

findings.text: This page is the site's front page, but almost all of it is about firstmate, not Athena. Someone who came to learn Athena gets two sentences about it and then a long technical study of a project they may never have heard of.
"Start here" explains firstmate and walks one task from start to finish clearly. A newcomer can follow the whole lifecycle before reaching the detailed cards.
findings.source: Firstmate is a tool for people who direct AI coding agents. It keeps a backlog of programming tasks and hands each one to a worker

findings.text: The page ends with clear next actions: links to install Athena, to learn about firstmate, and how to check a claim against its source. That answers "what do I do next".
The name "firstmate-work-handling" is never explained, so a newcomer won't know if it is a file, a job or a study name.
findings.source: This page is that study of firstmate, from firstmate-work-handling.

findings.text: Several terms are used without being defined: "home", "scout" (the glossary entry for ship only says it is "named next to scouts"), "endpoint", "secondmate" and "brief". A newcomer stalls on these.
findings.source: Spawning a task moves its backlog item to In flight in the same run, and refuses when this home has no item for the work.

findings.text: This limitation is about Athena's internal data format, and it describes something the page doesn't even show. It confuses a newcomer more than it helps them.
findings.source: f2 model-limit ... these transitions name the agent as a stand-in. That name does not mean the agent, or any code, checks a guard.

findings.text: The Counters entry lists transition ids before the reader has seen the transition cards, and it doesn't say which transitions take a place and which free one.
findings.source: • places-held, changed by transitions t1, t3, t4
